summary: Missing route propagation after VPC peering attachment causing agent heartbeat loss for private deployment
description: Issue summary: After establishing a VPC peering connection between CoreHealth's private VPC and Redwood Private control-plane VPC, agents in the customer's subnet began dropping heartbeats to the control-plane. Impact: Several customer inference jobs stalled for ~40 minutes; alerts fired for 3 service endpoints. The customer reported inability to create new model rollouts during the window. Environment: CoreHealth private deployment (managed VPC peering), prod, us-east-1. Timeline: 2026-03-12 08:10 UTC peering attached; 08:16 UTC agents started failing heartbeats; 08:45 UTC support engaged; 09:10 UTC first mitigation applied.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Establish VPC peering between a customer VPC and Redwood private control-plane VPC without route propagation enabled.
2) Launch a private deploy agent in a subnet that relies on peering routes to reach control-plane CIDR.
3) Observe agent logs for heartbeat failures and control-plane connection timeouts.
4) Verify route tables on both VPCs to confirm missing route entries for the peer CIDR.
observed_behavior: Customer agents log repeated connection timeouts to control-plane endpoints; control-plane metrics show connection count drop for that customer; traceroute from agent subnets terminates at peer attachment and does not reach control-plane IPs. No TLS handshake errors were observed — TCP connection cannot be established (timeouts).
expected_behavior: After peering attachment, route tables should contain explicit routes for the peer CIDRs so agent traffic can reach control-plane endpoints and heartbeats remain healthy.
logs_and_diagnostics:
- Agent log excerpt: "2026-03-12T08:18:03Z WARN heartbeat: dial tcp 10.20.5.12:443: i/o timeout"
- Traceroute from customer subnet: last hop shows * * * at 10.20.0.1 (peering attachment)
- AWS route table (customer VPC) at 08:12 UTC: no route for 10.200.0.0/16 (control-plane CIDR) to peering-attach-0a1b2c
- AWS VPC Peering status: Active, but Route Propagation toggle was left OFF by automation template
- Support console: control-plane received SYNs from other customers in region; only CoreHealth flows were blackholed.
investigation_notes:
08:20 UTC: Confirmed peering connection is Active.
Hypothesis A: Security group or NACL blocking return traffic — checked SGs and NACLs, none deny outbound to control-plane CIDR.
Hypothesis B: Route table missing entries for control-plane CIDR on customer side — verified missing.

08:35 UTC: Customer automation applied peering but did not add explicit routes. AWS console shows peering attachment ID peering-0a1b2c. Route propagation not applicable for peering; routes must be inserted manually.
09:02 UTC: Temporary mitigation: manually added route 10.200.0.0/16 -> peering-0a1b2c in customer route table; agent heartbeats recovered within ~90s.

Link to Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234ABC/p1678671123456
Link to VPC flow sample: s3://redwood-support-logs/corehealth/2026-03-12/vpcflow.log
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T09:15: Logged initial findings and requested customer confirmation before applying route. Customer approved manual route update.
Sofia Chen (Solutions) 2026-03-12T09:28: Noted our onboarding script didn't assert route insertion for peering when customers use their own infrastructure templates. Adding runbook step.
CoreHealth Ops (Customer) 2026-03-12T09:30: Confirmed agent heartbeats return to normal; production jobs resumed. Thanks for quick fix.
Liam Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-12T10:10: Will push infra PR to add validation that peering attachments are followed by route entries; tracking in INT-1123.
temporary_workaround: Manually insert route entries for the control-plane CIDR (10.200.0.0/16) pointing to the peering attachment in the customer's VPC route table. This restores agent connectivity immediately.
resolution: Root cause: Missing explicit route entries in the customer's VPC route table after VPC peering attachment. AWS VPC peering requires manual route addition; our customer onboarding automation and template did not enforce this step. Fix applied: 1) Manual route added by customer at 09:02 UTC which restored heartbeat; 2) Support opened INT-1123 for infra validation and added a runbook entry 'vpc-peering-route-check' to Confluence; 3) Created a new pre-deploy validation in the onboarding script to assert route presence and alert if absent. Follow-up: customer-runbook PR to include a step to verify routes, and engineering will add a monitoring alert for >1 minute heartbeat gaps tied to recent peering events.
postmortem_followup_actions: INT-1123: Add automated post-peering route validation to onboarding automation
Create CloudWatch synthetic check to validate agent-to-control-plane TCP reachability after peering events
Update private deployment checklist and Confluence runbook to require explicit route insertion proof
Reach out to CoreHealth to confirm completed runbook updates and offer a guided review session
